ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.claim: The angel taught the Prophet like an affectionate teacher, approaching and bending over his pupil, and the Prophet fully grasped the instruction rather than hearing unclear distant words.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.anchor: The Prophet (sws) fully grasped and understood this instruction

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r18.claim: In “He taught him,” the pronoun may refer to the Messenger, with “revelation” as an omitted second object, or to the Qur'an, with “the Messenger” as an omitted first object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r18.anchor: علمه: الضمير عائد على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، فالمفعول الثاني محذوف، أي علمه الوحي. أو على القرآن، فالمفعول الأول محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r19.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r19.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Rabīʿ identify the possessor of great strength as Gabriel, fitting the descriptions that follow.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r19.anchor: شديد القوى: هو جبريل، وهو مناسب للأوصاف التي بعده، وقاله ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r20.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r20.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the possessor of great strength as God; the author considers this interpretation far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p9/r20.anchor: وقال الحسن: شديد القوى: هو الله تعالى، وهو بعيد

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r1.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun in “he taught him” to refer to the revelation: the mighty in power taught the revelation, whether it is scripture or inspiration.
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r1.anchor: الضمير في { علمه } عائدا إلى الوحي

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r2.claim: Rāzī prefers that the pronoun refers to Muhammad: Gabriel, the mighty in power, taught the Prophet, the “companion” mentioned earlier; Gabriel’s intellectual and practical faculties are strong.
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r2.anchor: والأولى أن يقال الضمير عائد إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم تقديره علم محمد شديد القوى جبريل

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r3.claim: Praising the teacher also praises the student, making Muhammad’s distinction visible in a way that merely naming Gabriel as teacher would not.
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r3.anchor: أن مدح المعلم مدح المتعلم فلو قال علمه جبريل ولم يصفه ما كان يحصل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فضيلة ظاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r4.claim: Calling Gabriel mighty answers the opponents’ claim that Muhammad heard ancient tales during a trip to Syria: his teacher was no ordinary human.
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r4.anchor: فيه ردا عليهم حيث قالوا أساطير الأولين سمعها وقت سفره إلى الشام

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r5.claim: Gabriel’s perceptive power, memory, and integrity together warrant trust in his transmission, just as the description of the messenger in al-Takwīr combines strength, standing, and trustworthiness.
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r5.anchor: قوة الإدراك شرط الوثوق بقول القائل

RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r6.claim: The description consoles Muhammad: Gabriel can withstand divine communication; God may first teach through an intermediary and then directly, as in “He taught you what you did not know.”
RAZI-FULL:v28p245#2/r6.anchor: في تسلية النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:53:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r1.claim: Most commentators identify the one of awesome power as the Archangel Gabriel, who imparted revelation to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r1.anchor: The one of awesome power is understood by most commentators to be a reference to the Archangel Gabriel, who imparted the revelation to the Prophet (JJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:53:5/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r2.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r2.claim: Other commentators identify the one of awesome power as God Himself.
STUDYQURAN:53:5/r2.anchor: and by others as a reference to God Himself.

BURSEVI:v9p176/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p176/r1.claim: The author cites Rumi as presenting the Quran as guarded from error, neither astrology, geomancy, nor dreams, but divine revelation.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r1.anchor: نى نجومست ونى رملست ونه خواب

BURSEVI:v9p176/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r2.speaker: صوفيان
BURSEVI:v9p176/r2.claim: The Sufis call it heart-revelation: the heart is God's place of regard and, when aware, is guarded against error.

BURSEVI:v9p176/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p176/r3.claim: The cited saying that a believer sees by God's light supports the image of a heart protected from error and forgetfulness.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r3.anchor: مؤمنا ينظر بنور الله شدى از خطا وسهو ايمن آمدى

BURSEVI:v9p176/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p176/r4.claim: If waḥy means scripture, Gabriel taught by bringing it down, reciting, and explaining it; if it means inspiration, he taught by conveying it to the Prophet's heart, as in 26:193–194.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r4.anchor: هذا على أن يكون الوحي بمعنى الكتاب وإن كان بمعنى الإلهام فتعليمه بتبليغه إلى قلبه

BURSEVI:v9p176/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p176/r5.claim: The adjective is annexed to its agent, like ḥasan al-wajh; an omitted noun is understood, meaning an angel mighty in strength, Gabriel.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r5.anchor: من إضافة الصفة إلى فاعلها مثل حسن الوجه والموصوف محذوف أي ملك شديد قواه وهو جبريل

BURSEVI:v9p176/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p176/r6.claim: Gabriel's strength is illustrated by carrying Lot's towns from subterranean waters on a wing, bringing down Thamud with a cry, and blowing Iblis from the Holy Land to a distant Indian mountain.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r6.anchor: أنه قلع قرى قوم لوط من الماء الأسود الذي تحت الثرى وحملها على جناحه ورفعها إلى السماء

BURSEVI:v9p176/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p176/r7.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v9p176/r7.claim: Al-Raghib connects mirra with a tightly twisted cord; the dictionaries give it meanings including bodily strength, sound judgment, firmness, and a strong rope, and dhū mirra denotes Gabriel.
BURSEVI:v9p176/r7.anchor: قال الراغب : أمررت الحبل إذا فتلته

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r3.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Prophet, the Qur'an as revelation, or revelation generally; the second object of “taught” is omitted in each construction.
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r3.anchor: للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أو للقرآن بما هو وحي

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r4.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r4.claim: Commentators identify the one of mighty powers as Gabriel, whom God also describes as powerful.
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r4.anchor: والمراد بشديد القوى - على ما قالوا - جبريل

TABATABAI:53:3-7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r5.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the one of mighty powers as God.
TABATABAI:53:3-7/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد به هو الله سبحانه

TABRISI:53:1-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:1-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:1-10/r10.claim: Quwwa is ability rooted in strength; mirra first meant strong twisting and came to mean ability, so the terms overlap.
TABRISI:53:1-10/r10.anchor: والقوة القدرة وأصله الشدة وأصل المرة شدة الفتل ثم تجري المرة على القدرة

TABRISI:53:2-5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:2-5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع وقتادة
TABRISI:53:2-5/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Rabiʿ, and Qatada identify the teacher as Gabriel, powerful in himself and his created form; quwā is plural of quwwa.
TABRISI:53:2-5/r8.anchor: يعني جبرائيل ع أي القوي في نفسه وخلقته عن ابن عباس والربيع وقتادة

THALABI:v9p136/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p136/r4.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p136/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi illustrates Gabriel’s strength by saying he uprooted Lot’s towns from the black water, carried them on his wing, and overturned them.
THALABI:v9p136/r4.anchor: قال الكلبي: وكانت شدته أنه اقتلع قريات قوم لوط من الماء الأسود، وحملها على جناحه

THALABI:v9p136/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p136/r5.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p136/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says Gabriel once struck Iblis with his wing and cast him to a distant mountain in India.
THALABI:v9p136/r5.anchor: وكانت شدته أيضا أنه أبصر إبليس وهو يكلم عيسى على بعض عقاب الأرض المقدسة فنفحه بجناحه نفحة ألقاه في أقصى جبل بالهند

THALABI:v9p136/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p136/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p136/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi also counts Gabriel’s cry that left Thamud collapsed and extinguished as a sign of his strength.
THALABI:v9p136/r6.anchor: وكانت شدته أيضا صيحته بثمود فأصبحوا جاثمين خامدين

THALABI:v9p136/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p136/r7.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v9p136/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi adds Gabriel’s swift descent from heaven to the prophets and ascent back to heaven.
THALABI:v9p136/r7.anchor: وكانت شدته أيضا هبوطه من السماء على الأنبياء وصعوده إليها في أسرع من الطرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p12#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p12#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p12#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes identify the one who taught Muhammad as Gabriel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p12#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: يعني جبريل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r6.claim: The one who taught Muhammad is Gabriel.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:1-8/r6.anchor: علمه شديد القوى } أي: جبريل عليه السلام

QASHANI:53:1-6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:1-6/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:1-6/r5.claim: The one who taught him is the Spirit of Holiness, a spirit powerful enough to subdue and affect the levels beneath it.
QASHANI:53:1-6/r5.anchor: قاهر لما تحته من المراتب مؤثر فيها تأثيرا قويا

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r5.claim: Because taught takes two objects, one is omitted: either the Prophet is the object and Qur'an is implicit, or Qur'an is the object and the Prophet is implicit; the sense is the same.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r5.anchor: Tâlim etti ona “tâlim” fiili iki mef‘ûle ta‘addî eder. Bundan burada ya birinci veya ikinci mef‘ûlün mahzuf olduğunu anlarız.

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r6.claim: God is unquestionably the Qur'an's teacher, while Gabriel is the messenger who, by God's permission, brought and conveyed it to Muhammad's heart.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r6.anchor: Kur’ân’ı tâlim eden Allah teâlâ olduğunda şüphe yok ise de

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r7.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r7.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies the one described as strong in powers as God.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r7.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan vârid olan bir rivayete göre Allah teâlâ denilmiş ise de

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r8.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r8.claim: Aisha's report identifies Gabriel; many commentators prefer Gabriel because the wording and attributes suit him.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r8.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe’den vârid olan rivayette Cebrâil diye tefsir olunmuş ve evsâf ve elfâzın zâhiri de buna münâsib bulunmuş olduğundan çokları Cebrâil demişlerdir.

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r9.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r9.claim: Beyzavi calls him an angel of great powers, Gabriel, who mediates the manifestation of miracles.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r9.anchor: Beyzâvî مَلَكٌ شَدِيدٌ قـُوَاهُ وَهُوَ جَبـْرَائِيلُ فَإن َّهُ الْوَاسِطَةُ فِي إِبْدَاءِ الْخَوَارِقِ

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r10.speaker: Taberî
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r10.claim: Tabari glosses strong in powers as strong in means or resources.

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r11.speaker: Nîsâbûrî
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r11.claim: Nishaburi understands the phrase to mean that all of Gabriel's intellectual and practical powers are strong.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r11.anchor: Nîsâbûrî de “yani ilmî ve amelî kuvveleri hepsi şedîd” diye ifade etmiş

ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r12.speaker: Nîsâbûrî
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r12.claim: Nishaburi says praising the teacher highlights the pupil's excellence; the wording also rebuts claims that a human taught him, since humans are weak and have little knowledge.
ELMALILI:53:1-7#2/r12.anchor: Müte‘allimin fazileti anlaşılmak için muallim medholunmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.claim: The mysterious, vivid scene points to faith about what senses cannot reach and warns against straining reason beyond its limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.anchor: duyularla algılanamayan, fizik âlemin ötesine taşan konularda imanın esas olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.claim: The passage condemns pagan attempts to make divinity concrete through material or spiritual intermediaries and to ascribe godhood to beings besides God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka varlıklara tanrılık izâfe etme telakkisini mahkûm etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r4.claim: God is unquestionably the ultimate teacher of the Qur’an; the commentary invokes the statement that the Merciful taught the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r4.anchor: onu asıl öğretenin Cenâb-ı Hak olduğunda şüphe yoktur; Rahmân sûresinin 1-2. âyetinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r5.claim: God can also communicate revelation through a messenger, and the Qur’an identifies that messenger as Gabriel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r5.anchor: yüce Allah, Şûrâ sûresinin 51. âyetinde belirtildiği üzere vahyini elçi gönderip onun vasıtasıyla da bildirebilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r6.claim: The subject of “taught” has been taken either as God or as Gabriel.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r6.anchor: 5. âyette geçen “öğretti” anlamındaki fiilin öznesinin Allah Teâlâ veya Cebrâil olabileceği yorumları yapılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r7.claim: The flow of the passage and its chosen description make Gabriel the stronger candidate for the subject of “taught.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r7.anchor: ifade akışı ve özneyi nitelemek üzere seçilen kelimeler göz önüne alınarak ikinci ihtimal daha güçlü bulunmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r8.claim: Some exegetes say praise of the teacher highlights the learner’s merit and rejects unbelievers’ claim that a human taught Muhammad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r8.anchor: “öğreten” hakkında övgü ifadesi kullanılmasının öğrenenin faziletine dikkat çekme anlamı taşıdığı

QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r15.claim: The one of mighty powers who taught him is Gabriel.
QUSHAYRI:v3p247/r15.anchor: أي جبريل عليه السلام . و { ذو مرة } : أي ذو قوة وهو جبريل

AKHFASH:v2p526/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p526/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p526/r1.claim: Al-quwā is the plural of quwwa; he compares it with dialectal plural pairs such as ḥabwa/ḥuban and rashwa/rashan.
AKHFASH:v2p526/r1.anchor: جماعة "القوة" وبعض العرب يقول "حبوة" و"حبى" فينبغي أن يقول "القوى"

FARRA:v3p94/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p94/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p94/r6.claim: The one mighty in power is Gabriel; ذو مرة in the next verse describes him.
FARRA:v3p94/r6.anchor: أراد جبريل- صلى الله عليه- «ذو مرة» (6) من نعت شديد القوى

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r1.claim: The one described as mighty in power is Gabriel.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r2.claim: The root image is the strands of a rope; quwwah is one strand.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p427#3/r2.anchor: وأصله من "قوى الحبل"؛ وهي طاقاته. الواحدة: قوة.

MAJAZ:v2p235/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p235/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p235/r7.claim: Al-quwā is a collective term for strength.

NAHHAS:v4p265/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r7.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v4p265/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports a reading with kasra on qāf, based on the similarity of the patterns فعلة and فعلة.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r7.anchor: وحكى الفراء أنه يقرأ ( شديد القوى ) بكسر القاف

NAHHAS:v4p265/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p265/r8.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v4p265/r8.claim: Qatāda identifies the one strong in powers as Gabriel.
NAHHAS:v4p265/r8.anchor: قال قتادة شديد القوى جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم

SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r1.claim: The pronoun in علمه most apparently refers to the Messenger, with the second object omitted: the mighty one taught the Messenger the revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون هذه الهاء للرسول، وهو الظاهر، فيكون المفعول الثاني محذوفا

SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the Qur'an or revelation, and the first object, the Messenger, is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r2.anchor: وأن تكون للقرآن والوحي، فيكون المفعول الأول محذوفا أي: علمه الرسول.

SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r3.claim: شديد القوى most apparently refers to Gabriel; an alternative is God, supported by 55:1–2.
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r3.anchor: وشديد القوى: قيل: جبريل وهو الظاهر. وقيل: الباري تعالى لقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r4.claim: The adjective شديد is annexed to its nominative complement القوى in a non-genuine construct.
SAMIN-DURR:53:5/r4.anchor: وشديد القوى: من إضافة الصفة المشبهة لمرفوعها فهي غير حقيقية.

ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r3.claim: The one described as mighty in power is Gabriel.

ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r4.claim: The pronoun as the object of taught refers to the Prophet; Gabriel taught him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p70/r4.anchor: علم النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:1#n3/r1.claim: The mighty one who taught Muhammad is the Angel of Revelation, Gabriel.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.claim: Because inspiration can mean ordinary ilham to Moses’ mother, the bee, or humans and jinn, “علمه شديد القوى” identifies Gabriel as the revealer who taught Muhammad; God remains the ultimate teacher.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.anchor: فأراد سبحانه أن يقطع أي فكرة فقال (علّمه شديد القوى) بمعنى أنه ليس إلهاماً ولكنه وحي علّمه إياه شديد القوى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r2.claim: The form “علّمه” conveys sustained, repeated teaching, unlike “أعلّمه.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r2.anchor: وفعل علّمه تفيد المداومة والتكثير على خلاف أُعلّمه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r3.claim: The two attributes signify strength and knowledge, sound judgment, and precision needed for the ascent and for Gabriel to protect the Prophet and preserve revelation; crossing the heavens also requires “سلطان.”
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r3.anchor: هاتان الصفتان فيهما إشارة أن الخروج إلى أقطار السموات يحتاج إلى أمرين هما القوة والعلم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the Prophet and the omitted second object is Qur'an or revelation; Abu Hayyan alternatively takes it as Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r1.anchor: ( علمه ( الضمير للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Rabi identify the one mighty in power as Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r2.anchor: هو جبريل عليه السلام كما قال ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع

ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r3.claim: Alusi cites Gabriel's strength in lifting and overturning Lot's towns and bringing Thamud down with a cry.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r3.anchor: أنه قلع قرى قوم لوط من الماء الأسود الذي تحت الثرى وحملها على جناحه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r4.claim: Gabriel descended to and ascended from prophets faster than a blink, exceeding sunlight's speed.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p47/r4.anchor: وكان هبوطه على الأنبياء عليهم السلام وصعوده في أسرع من رجعة الطرف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p400/r4.claim: The one of mighty powers who taught him is Gabriel; القوى is the plural of قوة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r1.claim: The one of mighty powers is Gabriel, the intermediary in bringing about miracles.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r1.anchor: ملك شديد قواه وهو جبريل عليه السلام فإنه الواسطة في إبداء الخوارق

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r2.claim: A report says Gabriel uprooted and raised Lot's towns to heaven, overturned them, and gave Thamūd a cry that left them collapsed by morning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:5-8/r2.anchor: روي أنه قلع قرى قوم لوط ورفعها إلى السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r5.claim: The one who taught the Prophet the revelation was Gabriel, whose extraordinary power makes the Prophet’s instruction remarkable despite his being unlettered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r5.anchor: ولما كان الوحي ظاهرا فيما بواسطة الملك

BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r6.claim: Gabriel can carry out everything God commands, displaying a capacity greater than the Prophetic audience had seen.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p313#2/r6.anchor: فإن معلمه بهذه الصفة التي هو بها بحيث ينفذ كل ما أمره الله به

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#2/r1.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#2/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ identifies the one of great strength who taught Muhammad as Gabriel.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3318#2/r1.anchor: عن الربيع رضي الله عنه في قوله : علمه شديد القوى قال : جبريل .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r7.claim: The clause beginning 'taught him' starts a new explanatory passage about how revelation happened.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r7.anchor: وجملة { علمه شديد القوى } الخ ، مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لبيان كيفية الوحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r8.claim: The object pronoun in علمه may refer to revelation or the Qur'an denoted by هو in 53:4; it is the first object of علم, with an omitted second object meaning 'he taught it to your companion' from 53:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r8.anchor: وضمير الغائب في { علمه } عائد إلى الوحي ، أو إلى ما عاد إليه ضمير { هو }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r9.claim: Alternatively, the hāʾ in علمه refers to the Prophet, and the omitted object refers to revelation, refuting the claim that a human taught him in 16:103.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r9.anchor: ويجوز جعل هاء { علمه } عائدا إلى { صاحبكم } والمحذوف عائد إلى { وحي } إبطالا لقول المشركين { إنما يعلمه بشر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r10.claim: Here ʿallama takes two objects because it is the doubled form of ʿalima, which takes one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r10.anchor: و ( علم ) هنا متعد إلى مفعولين لأنه مضاعف ( علم ) المتعدي إلى مفعول واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r11.claim: شديد القوى modifies an omitted noun, 'angel,' supplied by the following description of angelic traits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r11.anchor: و { شديد القوى } : صفة لمحذوف يدل عليه ما يذكر بعد مما هو من شؤون الملائكة ، أي ملك شديد القوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r12.speaker: المفسرون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r12.claim: The exegetes unanimously identify the one of great strength as Gabriel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r12.anchor: واتفق المفسرون على أن المراد به جبريل عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r13.claim: Strength means the capacity to carry out God's commands in great intellectual and physical works; the angel brings revelation to the messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p94/r13.anchor: والمراد ب { القوى } استطاعة تنفيذ ما يأمر الله به من الأعمال العظيمة العقلية والجسمانية ، فهو الملك الذي ينزل على الرسل بالتبليغ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r9.claim: The pronoun in 'he taught him' could refer to the Quran, but it more likely refers to Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r9.anchor: والضمير في قوله: علمه يحتمل أن يكون للقرآن، والأظهر أنه لمحمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r10.speaker: قتادة والربيع وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r10.claim: Qatada, al-Rabiʿ, and Ibn Abbas identify the mighty teacher as Gabriel, who taught Muhammad the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r10.anchor: قتادة والربيع وابن عباس: هو جبريل عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r11.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the mighty teacher as God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن المعلم الشديد القوى هو الله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r12.claim: Al-quwā is the plural of quwwa; the description of power fits Gabriel, as the continuation indicates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p196/r12.anchor: والقوى جمع قوة، وهذا في جبريل مكتمن، ويؤيده قوله تعالى:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya's correct view is that all these descriptions concern Gabriel: 53:13 says Muhammad saw him on another descent, implying an earlier one, and no report says Muhammad saw God before the Night Journey. Seeing God with the heart remains possible.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p197/r2.anchor: والصحيح عندي أن جميع ما في هذه الآيات هو مع جبريل، بدليل قوله: ولقد رآه نزلة أخرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Ibn Amir use fatha at all verse endings; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission uses imāla on raʾā. Nafi and Abu Amr use an intermediate form; Hamza and al-Kisai use imāla throughout, while Abu Amr in Ubayd's transmission uses it for al-aʿlā and tadallā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر هذه السورة كلها بفتح أواخر آيها وأمال عاصم في رواية أبي بكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r1.claim: The one of mighty powers who taught the Prophet is Gabriel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r1.anchor: وهو جبريل عليه السلام علم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r2.claim: Ibn Qutaybah derives quwā from the strengths or strands of a rope; its singular is quwwa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p64/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة وأصل هذا من قوى الحبل وهي طاقاته الواحدة قوة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444/r1.claim: The one who taught Muhammad what he brought to people is Gabriel, as also described in 81:19–21.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p444/r1.anchor: وهو جبريل، عليه السلام، كما قال: {إنه لقول رسول كريم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r1.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r1.claim: Anas reports a vision in which Gabriel struck the Prophet's shoulders, they rose from a tree to the horizons, and the Prophet saw heaven open, great light, and a veil of pearl and ruby before receiving revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r1.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "بينا أنا قاعد إذ جاء جبريل، عليه السلام، فوكز بين كتفي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r2.speaker: أبو بكر البزار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r2.claim: Al-Bazzar says only al-Harith ibn Ubayd transmitted the Anas report, describing him as a well-known Basran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r2.anchor: ثم قال البزار: لا يرويه إلا الحارث بن عبيد، وكان رجلا مشهورا من أهل البصرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Ma'in judged al-Harith ibn Ubayd to be nothing reliable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r3.anchor: إلا أن ابن معين ضعفه، وقال: ليس هو بشيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r4.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r4.claim: Ahmad called al-Harith ibn Ubayd's hadith troubled.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r5.claim: Abu Hatim said al-Harith's material may be written down but is not suitable as proof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم الرازي: كتب حديثه ولا يحتج به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r6.speaker: ابن حبان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r6.claim: Ibn Hibban says al-Harith made many errors and cannot be relied on when he is the sole transmitter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r6.anchor: وقال ابن حبان: كثر وهمه فلا يجوز الاحتجاج به إذا انفرد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the Anas report one of al-Harith's unusual narrations, notes objectionable wording and an extraordinary account, and suggests it may have been a dream.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r7.anchor: فهذا الحديث من غرائب رواياته، فإن فيه نكارة وغرابة ألفاظ وسياقا عجيبا، ولعله منام، والله أعلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r8.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r8.claim: Abdullah reports that the Prophet saw Gabriel with six hundred wings, each covering the horizon and shedding pearls, rubies, and other marvels; Ahmad alone transmits this version.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل في صورته وله ستمائة جناح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet asked to see Gabriel in his created form; a dark mass rose from the east, the Prophet fainted, and Gabriel revived him and wiped his mouth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p445/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جبريل أن يراه في صورته، فقال: ادع ربك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p446/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p446/r1.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p446/r1.claim: The preceding report from Ibn Abbas about the Prophet fainting at Gabriel's appearance is transmitted by Ahmad alone.

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r11.claim: Quwwa means ability and originally denotes strength.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r11.anchor: والقوة: القدرة، وأصله الشدة، والجمع: القوى

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r1.claim: The one of mighty powers who taught Muhammad is Gabriel, by consensus.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p391/r1.anchor: علمه شديد القوى } يعني : جبريل في قول الجميع

MUQATIL:53:3-9/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r2.claim: The one of great strength is Gabriel, powerful in every respect.
MUQATIL:53:3-9/r2.anchor: يعني القوة في كل شىء، يعني جبريل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r2.speaker: الجمهور
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r2.claim: The mighty in power is Gabriel, according to the majority; the genitive is not a true possessive but a construction of an intensive adjective with its agent.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r2.anchor: ﴿ شديد القوى ﴾ ملك شديد قواه والاضافة غير حقيقة لانها اضافة الصفة المشبهة إلى فاعلها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r3.claim: Gabriel's strength is illustrated by uprooting Lot's towns from the dark water, carrying them on his wing to heaven and overturning them, and by a cry that left Thamud dead.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188/r3.anchor: ومن قوته انه اقتلع قرى قوم لوط من الماء الاسود وحملها على جناحه ورفعها إلى السماء ثم قلبها وصاح صيحة بثمود فأصبحوا جاثمين

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the one of great power who taught Muḥammad as Gabriel.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r1.anchor: يعني جبريل عليه السلام في قول سائر المفسرين سوى الحسن فإنه قال: هو الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the one who taught him as God.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r2.anchor: في قول سائر المفسرين سوى الحسن فإنه قال: هو الله عز وجل

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r16.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r16.claim: Al-Kalbī recounts Gabriel’s strength: he uprooted Lot’s towns, carried them to heaven on a wing, and overturned them.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r16.anchor: قال الكلبي: وكان من شدة جبريل عليه السلام: أنه اقتلع مدائن قوم لوط من الأرض السفلى، فحملها على جناحه حتى رفعها إلى السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r17.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r17.claim: Al-Kalbī says Gabriel struck Iblīs with a wing while he spoke to Jesus, throwing him to a distant mountain in India.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r17.anchor: وكان من شدته أيضا: أنه أبصر إبليس يكلم عيسى عليه السلام على بعض عقاب من الأرض المقدسة فنفحه بجناحه نفحة ألقاه بأقصى جبل في الهند

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r18.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r18.claim: Al-Kalbī says Gabriel’s shout killed the numerous people of Thamūd, leaving them motionless and extinguished.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r18.anchor: وكان من شدته: صيحته بثمود في عددهم وكثرتهم، فأصبحوا جاثمين خامدين

QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r19.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r19.claim: Al-Kalbī adds that Gabriel descended to prophets and returned to heaven faster than a glance.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:5-7/r19.anchor: وكان من شدته: هبوطه من السماء على الأنبياء وصعوده إليها في أسرع من الطرف
